stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The mention of 'transformers' and 'safetensors' indicates relevance to modern ML infrastructure.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest large language models.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and features native support for image input via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on accessible LLM deployment.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for persistent AI agents.
The model is designed for complex, multi-step tasks requiring context gathering and tool use on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly growing, serving a large developer base of 8.9 million.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when running coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability for these AI agents to run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Microsoft discloses Azure revenue as part of major financial reporting changes
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is restructuring its financial reporting by splitting its business segments.
The company is disclosing Azure cloud revenue for the first time in quarterly reports.
These changes are intended to better reflect the operational impact of AI on Microsoft's business.

stories.title: Anker announces its first over-the-counter hearing aids
stories.author: John.Higgins
bullet_points: Anker is entering the hearing aid market with its first over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids.
This launch comes at a timely moment, following the exit of major US OTC manufacturers like Eargo and Lexie Hearing.
The move signals a potential significant shift in the accessible hearing aid market.

stories.title: Anker’s new MindBase is an AI-powered brain for your smart home
stories.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
bullet_points: Anker is launching the Eufy MindBase, a new AI hub for smart home security.
The device utilizes an on-device, proprietary LLM to process footage locally.
This local processing ensures user footage never leaves the home, emphasizing privacy.

stories.title: FCC plans robocall scorecard to grade phone companies on spam call blocking
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: The FCC is planning to introduce a robocall scorecard system for phone carriers.
This scorecard will evaluate carriers based on their performance in blocking spam calls.
Metrics for the score may include call-blocking statistics and customer complaint data.

stories.title: US court rules Google will not have to sell ad exchange after losing antitrust case
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: US court ruled against Google in an antitrust case concerning its ad exchange.
The Department of Justice (DOJ) successfully proved Google engaged in illegal practices.
However, the court decision did not force Google to divest its ad exchange, limiting the DOJ's desired outcome.

stories.title: The Army just used a 20-kilowatt laser to take out three drones
stories.author: Fernanda González, wired.com
bullet_points: The U.S. Army has deployed a 20-kilowatt laser system.
The system is capable of tracking and destroying hostile drones.
This represents a significant advancement in directed energy weapons for defense applications.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on enhancing Large Language Models (LLMs) for high-level competitive programming, benchmarking against IOI and ICPC.
A specialized pipeline combining problem curation, synthetic reasoning traces, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL) is introduced.
The study compares two models, Nemotron-3-Nano-CC (SFT+RL) and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC (SFT only), trained on 22,000 curated problems.

stories.title: The Implications of Linguistic Illegibility for LLM Security
stories.author: James Mickens
bullet_points: Introduces the concept of 'linguistic illegibility' in LLMs.
Argues that externalized language outputs and extracted features are unreliable proxies for internal model computation.
Highlights a fundamental challenge in interpreting and understanding how Large Language Models actually function.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: Researchers developed an end-to-end pipeline (SFT + RL) to specialize LLMs for competitive programming.
The model, Nemotron-3-Nano-CC, achieved high performance using both SFT and RL on 22,000 curated problems.
The work addresses the challenge of testing LLM reasoning capabilities in highly rigorous settings like IOI and ICPC.

stories.title: Untangling the Mechanisms of Misleading Context in Medical Question Answering
stories.author: Noémie Elhadad
bullet_points: Investigates how misleading context corrupts the expert-level medical judgment of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The research examines the model's susceptibility, disclosure, reasoning mechanisms, and monitorability when presented with flawed medical context.
Uses the MedMisBench dataset to empirically test and understand the failure modes of LLMs in critical medical QA tasks.

stories.title: Repo-To-Skill: Distilling GitHub Repositories Into AI4AI Skills
stories.author: Zheng Liu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in autonomous AI agents: the lack of operational, domain-specific knowledge needed to translate theoretical ML methods into working implementations.
It proposes 'Repo-To-Skill,' a method to distill practical, expert knowledge embedded within GitHub repositories into usable AI skills.
This work aims to bridge the gap between high-level agent architectures (planning, execution) and the granular, practical know-how found in real-world codebases.

stories.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber
stories.author: bratao
bullet_points: Announcement of Gemini 3.8 Flash, indicating a new iteration in Google's Gemini model family.
The release suggests an emphasis on 'Flash' capabilities, likely pointing towards improved speed and efficiency for deployment.
The news originates from DeepMind/Google, placing it at the forefront of major AI development.

stories.title: Google avoids a breakup of its ad tech business
stories.author: donohoe
bullet_points: Google successfully defended against a U.S. bid to force the divestiture of its ad tech business.
The legal victory suggests a significant regulatory hurdle for antitrust actions against Google's advertising ecosystem.
This outcome impacts the ongoing scrutiny of Big Tech's market dominance in digital advertising.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Here’s the first 4K 120Hz UST projector with optical lens shift
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: Awol Vision has released the LuxVision, a new Ultra-Short Throw (UST) projector.
Key features include 4K resolution, 120Hz refresh rate, and optical lens shift for precise image placement.
The projector boasts high brightness (6000 ISO Lumens) and can project a 120-inch image from a very short distance (7.5 inches).

stories.title: Anker’s sleep speaker uses radar and flower power to help you relax
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: Anker's SleepLab speaker monitors sleep metrics (heart rate, breathing) without requiring a wearable device.
The device utilizes millimeter-wave radar (60GHz) placed on the nightstand to track subtle body movements.
The product aims to enhance sleep quality by providing continuous monitoring and personalized feedback.

stories.title: Anker’s Soundcore is bringing its incredible call quality to more headphones
stories.author: John.Higgins
bullet_points: Anker's Soundcore is expanding the use of its proprietary Thus processing chip across more audio products.
The Thus chip is highlighted for delivering superior call quality by effectively minimizing ambient background noise.
The technology was initially showcased with the Liberty 5 Pro series earbuds and was presented at IFA.

stories.title: I rented a car, and within hours, my driver's license was for sale
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A massive, real-time data breach is reportedly under FBI investigation.
The breach is linked to the compromise of personal data, exemplified by a driver's license being put up for sale.
The story highlights the severe risks associated with large-scale data security failures.

stories.title: Wary of Artemis IV timeline, NASA is changing lunar spacesuit design
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is modifying the design of lunar spacesuits.
The changes are being driven by concerns regarding the Artemis IV mission timeline.
Requirements are being adjusted to better suit near-term mission objectives.

stories.title: Google releases Gemini 3.8 Flash, its third Flash model in six weeks
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Flash, continuing its rapid deployment of Flash models.
The release suggests a continued focus on iterative, faster model updates rather than major Pro model overhauls at this time.
The frequency of these Flash releases indicates an aggressive pace of AI iteration from Google.

stories.title: Trump may be forced to reveal secret rules feds use for AI safety testing
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A lawsuit alleges that Trump's reviews of frontier AI models may conceal corruption.
The core issue involves the potential need for Trump to disclose secret rules governing federal AI safety testing.
The story touches upon the intersection of political oversight, AI regulation, and potential misuse of power.

stories.title: Is Russia's rival to Starlink failing? Here's what we know.
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The article discusses potential failures within Rassvet, a satellite constellation positioned as a rival to Starlink.
Initial data suggests at least three of the first 32 Rassvet satellites have experienced outright failures.
The news points to ongoing concerns regarding the operational status and reliability of the competing satellite system.

stories.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
stories.author: Roei Herzig
bullet_points: Current web agents utilize world models for action selection by predicting future web states.
These models are often trained using supervised next-state prediction, generating fixed representations like HTML snapshots.
The core issue is a misalignment: the training objective (next-state prediction) does not support the downstream ranker's need for discriminative state representations.

stories.title: Towards Trustworthy Autonomous Robots: An Explainable AI-Based Decision Framework
stories.author: Cagri Temel
bullet_points: Addresses the critical auditability challenge in deep learning-powered autonomous robots.
Introduces TRACE, a framework designed to trace every robot action back to sensor evidence via causal chains.
Organizes the decision-making process into four distinct, auditable layers, starting with Semantic Perception.

stories.title: Large Language Models (LLMs) for Telecom Root Cause Analysis (RCA): A Structured Reasoning Framework for Evidence-Grounded Diagnosis
stories.author: Zhang
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in complex 5G/6G telecom networks, which is hampered by cross-layer dependencies.
It proposes a structured reasoning framework to leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) for telecom RCA.
The research aims to mitigate common LLM weaknesses in this domain, such as hallucination and unstable reasoning, by grounding diagnoses in structured network evidence.

stories.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
stories.author: Suproteem Sarkar
bullet_points: The research investigates the coherence of probabilistic forecasts generated by large language models (LLMs).
It addresses the growing trend of users relying on LLMs for high-stakes life decisions (e.g., economic or disaster predictions).
The evaluation procedure builds upon de Finetti's theorem to test whether LLMs operate within a coherent world model.

stories.title: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
stories.author: Dongrui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SafeEvolve, a novel method for safety alignment in LLM-based agents.
Addresses the dual safety risks arising from both final LLM responses and multi-step execution trajectories.
Proposes a co-evolutionary approach that jointly shapes the base model and the interaction harness using agent experience.

stories.title: Measurement-Driven Sub-Network Selection for On-Premise Retrieval-Augmented Factory Agents
stories.author: Athanasios Bachoumis
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of deploying large language models (LLMs) for on-premise factory AI assistants due to hardware constraints.
Proposes a novel approach where model selection is treated as a post-adaptation problem, rather than relying solely on model size.
Demonstrates that general model capability and retrieval-augmented answer quality decouple from parameter count after structural compression and adaptation.

stories.title: A Common Measure of Communication for Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces
stories.author: Oiwi Parker Jones
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical lack of standardization in Speech Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs).
Current BCI research suffers from incomparable results due to variations in datasets, recording methods, and speech types.
Establishing a common measure of communication is presented as a necessary step for advancing the field and enabling better human-computer interaction.

stories.title: Discriminative World Models for Web Agents
stories.author: Roei Herzig
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical misalignment in current web agent world models, where supervised next-state prediction fails to generate discriminative states.
Existing web agents use world models to sample and rank candidate actions based on predicted future web states (e.g., HTML snapshots).
The research suggests that the training objective for world models needs to be changed to better serve the downstream ranking/reward models.

stories.title: Graph Machine: Towards Better Pretraining via Edges
stories.author: Lintai Hou
bullet_points: Introduces 'Graph Machine' (GM), a new architecture designed for improved pretraining.
GM maintains an $O(n)$-sized state accessible via sparse, dynamic routing, overcoming limitations of fixed-size states.
The core innovation involves using differentiable, pointer-like 'edges' for state access, replacing a large portion of dense Transformer layers.

stories.title: GRADSOLVE: fast exact gradients for ODE ensembles on GPUs
stories.author: Alessio Spurio Mancini
bullet_points: The research addresses a critical bottleneck in scientific computing: obtaining fast, exact gradients for ODE ensembles running on GPUs.
Current GPU solvers force a trade-off between computational speed (for ensembles) and differentiability (for gradient calculation).
GRADSOLVE introduces a novel method to achieve fast reverse-mode differentiation for ODE ensembles on GPUs.

stories.title: Improved Gradient Descent Lower Bounds Beyond Nesterov
stories.author: Kaizhao Liu
bullet_points: The research presents new lower bounds for accelerating gradient descent in smooth convex optimization.
It establishes a new non-anytime lower bound of $\Omega(n^{-1.6342})$ and an anytime lower bound of $\Omega(n^{-1.2408})$.
These bounds surpass previous state-of-the-art theoretical limits set by other researchers in the field.

stories.title: UE5M3 FP4 Block Scaling for Stable Language Model Pretraining
stories.author: Paul Balanca
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of 4-bit floating-point (FP4) pretraining in language models due to limited magnitude range.
The proposed solution pairs E2M1 payloads with unsigned E5M3 block scales to achieve a wider dynamic range.
This method allows for periodic tensor scaling, contrasting with existing techniques like NVIDIA's Transformer Engine recipe.

stories.title: User Feedback Provides a Unique Signal that LLMs Can not Detect
stories.author: Omri Abend
bullet_points: The research proposes that naturally occurring user feedback is a highly actionable learning signal for LLMs.
It challenges the prevailing view that user feedback is inherently too noisy or difficult to leverage.
The study suggests that the perceived ineffectiveness of user feedback is due to systematic biases in current LLM evaluation methods.

stories.title: Post-Training Language Models for Gold-Medal Performance in Coding Competitions
stories.author: Boris Ginsburg
bullet_points: The research focuses on specializing large language models (LLMs) for high-level competitive programming tasks (e.g., IOI, ICPC).
A novel pipeline combining problem curation, synthetic reasoning traces, Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), and Reinforcement Learning (RL) is introduced.
The study compares model performance using different training regimes (SFT vs. SFT+RL) on specialized model variants (Nemotron-3-Nano-CC and Nemotron-3-Ultra-CC).

stories.title: Dutch Books for Language Models
stories.author: Suproteem Sarkar
bullet_points: The paper investigates the coherence of probabilistic forecasts generated by language models (LLMs).
It addresses the growing user reliance on LLMs for high-stakes life decisions, such as economic or disaster predictions.
The evaluation method builds upon de Finetti's theorem to test the underlying world model consistency of the LLMs.

stories.title: DiscoSign: Discourse-Aware Text to Sign Language Gloss Translation
stories.author: Colin Lea
bullet_points: Introduces DiscoSign, a new computational approach for text to sign language gloss translation.
The system is discourse-aware, addressing limitations of traditional sentence-level sign language processing.
It utilizes a modular Large Language Model (LLM) framework to handle phenomena like spatial coreference resolution.

stories.title: EarlyEval: Cheaper Agent Evaluation via Early Outcome Prediction
stories.author: Xiaodong Gu
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of evaluating Large Language Model (LLM) agents, which can be prohibitively expensive.
Introduces 'EarlyEval,' a method based on early outcome prediction to reduce evaluation expenses.
Offers a complementary approach to existing benchmark distillation techniques, aiming to lower the cost of iterative agent development.

stories.title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
stories.author: Jun Yu
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of using Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) for continuous streaming video understanding.
Proposes 'ShallowStream,' a method that indexes shallowly before performing deep analysis to optimize processing.
Highlights the critical real-world applications of efficient streaming video understanding, such as autonomous driving and industrial monitoring.

stories.title: HyperStyler: Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer via Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks
stories.author: Chiehyeon Lim
bullet_points: Introduces 'HyperStyler,' a new method for Low-resource Authorship Style Transfer (LAST).
Addresses limitations in existing methods where static author embeddings fail to capture context-dependent stylistic variation.
Utilizes Context-aware Style Navigation and Hypernetworks to improve both style fidelity and semantic preservation with few examples.

stories.title: Muse Spark 1.3
stories.author: bvaldivielso
bullet_points: Meta has released an update to its Muse Spark model (version 1.3).
The announcement is posted on Meta AI Research's official blog.
This indicates ongoing development and iteration in Meta's generative AI capabilities.

stories.title: AI Code Validation
stories.author: mjodeh
bullet_points: The article discusses the capability of coding agents.
These agents can perform complex development tasks like modifying APIs and database logic.
Functionality includes generating tests and providing code explanations.
